method: Byte-offset-precise matching: each site's byte offset (recomputed from its shape-pattern match on the MASKED line, then read off the raw line at that column) is looked up against every CallClaim's [start_byte, end_byte) span across the whole package, via `girder analyze --json` + `girder inspect --json`'s call_evidence_v1 attribute. A module-level coverage-gap claim whose span covers the site counts as an honest disclosure (observed Unknown) UNLESS its reason is implicit-runtime-dispatch-not-certified, which is attached unconditionally to every Python module and would otherwise make every offset in every file always covered, collapsing unsafe_exclusion to permanently unreachable -- mirrors Rust's own NEVER_COVERS treatment of its analogous whole-file gap exactly. duplicate-semantic-path IS treated as a legitimate covering claim, matching Rust's own methodology note that it counts as honest disclosure, not a silent drop.

unsafe_exclusion_sites.root_cause: The enclosing function's call_evidence_v1 has claims for the two calls in the function (Model.model_construct(...) and m.model_dump()) but NONE for the `m.a == 3` comparison expression between them -- Girder's Python extractor does not emit a CallClaim for this binary_expression at all, not even an Unknown one. The always-present whole-module implicit-runtime-dispatch-not-certified claim exists but is correctly excluded from counting as coverage (see method note), so nothing covers this byte offset.

Same root cause as the pydantic site: no per-site CallClaim exists for this comparison expression, and this file has no duplicate-semantic-path claim (unlike 8 of the other 10 operator_dunder sites in this sample) to coincidentally cover it.

headline_finding: 0 overclaim (no false Must/May anywhere) but 2 unsafe_exclusion: two operator/comparison expressions get NO call evidence at all, not even a conservative Unknown claim. Root-caused, not guessed: Girder's Python extractor simply does not emit a CallClaim for a binary_expression used as a bare statement/assert argument in these two cases. 8 of 10 operator_dunder sites in this sample score 'exact' (observed Unknown) only because their files ALSO happen to carry an unrelated duplicate-semantic-path claim spanning the whole module -- not because operator dispatch itself is evidenced. Recall is 0%: all 13 true Must sites score conservative (Girder currently proves no cross-file/class-hierarchy Must binding for Python at all, matching the known same-file/top-level-only Rust limitation before Stage 3 Rust resolver work began). 0 May sites in this sample -- disclosed as a property of the specific 105-site sample, not assumed to generalize.

root_cause_tally.method: Derived from source facts per site (class hierarchies read directly in the extracted packages, not inferred from Girder's reason string), matching Rust's audit-correction.md's own discipline.

cross_file_or_class_hierarchy_must_not_a.description: All 13 true-Must sites require either a cross-file import resolution (e.g. deprecated_from_orm imported into a test file) or a class-hierarchy override check (self.fail(...), self._apply_single_annotation(...), Model.model_rebuild()) that Girder's current Python extractor does not attempt -- it proves only same-file, non-dispatch bindings (python-binding-or-dispatch-unproven is the observed reason on all 13).

operator_dispatch_never_evidenced_per_si.fraction: 2/10 operator_dunder sites scored (8/10 covered coincidentally via duplicate-semantic-path)
operator_dispatch_never_evidenced_per_si.description: No CallClaim is ever emitted for a binary_expression itself; the 8 sites that scored exact did so only because an unrelated whole-module duplicate-semantic-path claim happened to also be present in those specific files.
